newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds slow, but waiting nears an end.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds slow, but waiting nears an end.

text.p: *Australian bonds flat to firmer in light trade as market prepares for a week dominated by policy meetings of the Reserve Bank of Australia and the U.S. FOMC.

Australian bonds opened the week flat to firmer in slow trade, with the market continuing its wait ahead of policy meetings of the Reserve Bank of Australia on Tuesday and the U.S. FOMC on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Local markets also have their first major data in a number of weeks, with Wednesday's release of May retail trade and building approvals data.
In the lead up, however, traders said the local market was likely to remain slow, but well-supported by expectations that the RBA could cut rates during July.
"Obviously with the RBA board meeting and the FOMC, it's hard to see us racing one way or the other today," one trader said.

A Reuters survey of analysts on Friday found a 52.5 percent chance of a rate cut in July, with the market likely to be bought ahead of the 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time of any policy changes on both Wednesday and Thursday.
Even if the RBA does not move this week the front end is expected to remain well-supported on expectations an easing may come later in the month after second quarter inflation and wages data.

Spreads generally wider, although short end continues to narrow to Canada after last week's rate hike there. Weak NZ March quarter GDP data this mornig is expected to keep NZ debt firm, and may see spreads narrow further.
